old_title: Middle East live: Trump says Saudi nuclear deal contingent on normalising relations with Israel
new_title: UN chief says Middle East conflict is at the 'edge of the imaginable'
old_text:
Middle East live: Trump says Saudi nuclear deal contingent on normalising relations with Israel
President Donald Trump on Thursday said a civil nuclear deal between the US and Saudi Arabia is "totally subject" to Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords. Trump also threatened Yemen's Houthis with "major military punishment" for attacking two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and said he would hold Iran responsible for any Houthi attacks. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
Israeli civilian kills two West Bank Palestinians behind stabbing, army says
An Israeli civilian killed two Palestinians in the occupied West Bank after they allegedly stabbed another Israeli who was trying to extinguish a wildfire near a settlement, the military said.
Violence in the West Bank, a Palestinian territory occupied by Israel since 1967, has escalated since the start of the war in Gaza.
"Earlier today, a fire broke out in the area adjacent to the community of Itamar. During the extinguishing attempts, two terrorists stabbed an Israeli civilian," the military said.
It added that another Israeli identified the attack and "eliminated" the two Palestinians, without specifying how they were killed.
The wounded Israeli was stabbed in the chest and evacuated to hospital in serious condition, health officials said.
Trump says US will hold Iran accountable for Houthi attacks
President Donald Trump has posted another message on his Truth Social platform, this time threatening Yemen's Houthi militants, who said they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis had acted responsibly since US targeted them a year ago for attacking commercial shipping, said Trump. "Unfortunately, now they are starting up again, shooting at two Saudi Arabian ships last night. Please let this TRUTH serve to represent that if they do this again, the U.S. will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis, themselves ...," he wrote.
Trump says Saudi nuclear deal contingent on recognising Israel
President Donald Trump has said the nuclear deal between the US and Saudi Arabia signed Wednesday is contingent on the Gulf kingdom recognising Israel.
The deal to establish a civilian nuclear programme in the Gulf country "will be approved, but is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords," Trump said on his Truth Social platform.
Kuwait says drone attack hits Abdali border crossing with Iraq
Kuwait's army has said the Abdali border crossing with Iraq was hit by a drone attack, causing material damage but no casualties.
Located in Kuwait's northern Al-Jahra Province, Abdali is the country's main land border crossing with Iraq and a key route for passenger and commercial traffic between the two countries.
EU urges Houthis to stop attacks in Red Sea
Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen must cease all actions that endanger international shipping and the lives of seafarers, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Thursday.
Recent threats by Yemen's Houthis to impose a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia "pose a direct threat to regional stability and constitute a dangerous escalation", Kallas said in a statement.
The Houthis on Thursday said they struck two Saudi oil tankers as part of a blockade on Saudi Arabia, threatening to create a second chokepoint on global oil supplies alongside the Strait of Hormuz.
Kallas said such attacks were "unacceptable" and inflamed the already fragile situation in the region.
"Navigation must be unimpeded, in the Strait of Hormuz as well as in the Red Sea," the EU's top diplomat said.
UK withdraws remaining diplomats from Iran
Britain said on Friday it had withdrawn remaining diplomatic staff from Iran as the conflict between Iran and the United States escalates.
"Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran. Our embassy continues to operate remotely," the Foreign Office said on its website.
Britain in June withdrew its embassy staff from Iran, following in the footsteps of other European nations as well as Australia and New Zealand.
The withdrawals came after Israel launched renewed air strikes on Iran claiming its arch enemy was on the verge of developing a nuclear weapon.
Kremlin declines comment on report that Russia may have helped Iran strike CIA facilities in Gulf
The Kremlin on Thursday declined to comment on a Reuters report that US intelligence analysts were investigating possible Russian assistance in Iranian drone attacks on CIA facilities in the Gulf.
Four people familiar with US intelligence told Reuters that the officials had not yet reached firm conclusions about the possible Russian involvement in the attacks on CIA facilities.
But they cited the strikes' effectiveness and apparent precision, as well as Russia's broader technical support for Iran, as possible evidence.
Oman says it is working with Saudi Arabia, Yemeni parties and UN to resume political track to stability
Oman said on Thursday it is coordinating with Saudi Arabia, Yemeni parties and the UN special envoy for Yemen to resume the political track aimed at achieving security and stability in the region, according to a foreign ministry statement.
The ministry also stressed the need to avoid escalation and any threats that could worsen the situation in the Red Sea and endanger freedom of navigation.
Marco Rubio addresses Middle East and Ukraine conflicts • FRANCE 24 English
Watch again as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio addresses the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine at the end of the ASEAN summit in Manila.
Jordan army says it intercepted Iranian missiles, drones
Jordan said on Thursday that it had intercepted Iranian missiles and drones, as Tehran responded to US air strikes by hitting Washington's allies in the region.
The Jordanian army said in a statement it had intercepted three missiles on Thursday morning, while a fourth landed in an uninhabited area, and that it had intercepted six drones on Wednesday evening, with no casualties or material damage.
Iran army vows to continue strikes so long as country is under attack
The Iranian army said Thursday that it would continue its strikes around the region until the attacks on Iran stopped, state television reported.
"The armed forces' retaliatory attacks will continue as long as the US attacks on the country's infrastructure and coastal areas continue," said army spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia according to state TV, adding that the country was ready for "every enemy scenario".
EasyJet profit slides on Iran war impact as suitors circle
Takeover target easyJet on Thursday said third-quarter profit slumped 70 percent, bruised by volatile fuel prices and a travel-wary consumer due to chaos caused by the Iran war, but indicated somewhat clearer skies heading into peak summer.
The budget airline reported an £85 million ($113.8 million) profit for the three months to June 30, a far cry from the £286 million it logged last year. Results of easyJet, and rival Ryanair earlier this week.
The British airline said, however, that consumer confidence was increasing into the peak summer period and there was strong demand from travellers booking tickets closer to the date of travel.
"As consumer confidence increases, we are seeing the load factor gap close for peak summer and an extension of the booking curve," CEO Kenton Jarvis said in a statement.
Oil prices rise for a fifth day on supply concerns amid chokepoint threats
Oil prices rose for a fifth day on Thursday on increasing concerns about supply availability amid attacks on tankers in the Red Sea by Yemen's Houthis and strikes between the US and Iran that have once again nearly shut the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude futures rose $2.42, or 2.6 percent, to $96.49 by 06:40 GMT, the highest since June 8, having settled up more than $3 at $94.07 in the previous session, just shy of a six-week high.
US West Texas Intermediate crude climbed $1.59, or 1.8 percent, to $88.42, after Wednesday's rise of 3 percent.
Iran Guards destroy US military equipment in Jordan
Iran's Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the country's military, said on Thursday that they had attacked and destroyed several American military assets in Jordan.
The targets included a radar for the US THAAD missile defence system, a Patriot system, a C-RAM radar and a helicopter hangar, according to a statement from the Guards aired by state TV.
Iran's army says it attacked US bases in Kuwait, according to state media
Iran's army and its Revolutionary Guards on Thursday said they attacked several US bases in Kuwait following attacks by American forces on Iran.
The Guards claimed attacks on Ali Al Salem base, Camp Udairi and a telecommunications tower, while the army said it targeted Camp Doha, Ali Al Salem base and Camp Arifjan, according to separate statements by the forces carried by state TV.
Saudi Arabia confirms vessel hit in Red Sea by Houthi rebels
A vessel belonging to a Saudi company was hit while transiting the Red Sea, Saudi state media reported on Thursday, citing an official source, after Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed they had struck tankers in the waterway.
The source, quoted by the state-run Saudi Press Agency, said "the vessel ENCELIA, belonging to a Saudi company, was targeted while sailing in the Red Sea, resulting in a fire at the bow of the ship", but that all crew members were safe.
Iran says it stopped three tankers in Strait of Hormuz
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Thursday they stopped three oil tankers from passing through the Strait of Hormuz, as the United States and Iran vie for control over the vital waterway.
In recent weeks, Iran has hit tankers using a route hugging the Omani coast to traverse the strait, in a bid to strong-arm vessels into using its own waters and paying for safe passage.
"Three oil tankers, provoked and tempted by the child-killing American army, were trying to pass through the mine-laid route south of the Strait of Hormuz, but after one of them exploded and caught fire, the other two quickly turned around and turned back," the Guards said in a statement quoted by Iranian state media.
The statement did not say when the incident happened.
"The powerful IRGC Navy emphasises that the Strait of Hormuz is under our control... and any ship that is deceived by the US and intends to pass without coordination with the Islamic Republic of Iran will suffer the same fate," the Guards added.
Houthis say they targeted two Saudi oil tankers
Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday they had carried out a military operation targeting two Saudi oil tankers, identified as ENCELA and LAYLIA, saying the vessels violated a naval blockade imposed by the group.
The Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, drawing a warning from the Saudi-led coalition that it would respond "firmly", in a move that threatens to disrupt global energy supplies beyond the Gulf.
• President Donald Trump attended a dignified transfer of remains ceremony at a military base in Delaware for four US service members killed in the Iran war. Of the four slain soldiers, three were killed in an Iranian missile attack on a military base in Jordan and another died in a separate incident in northern Iraq.
• Trump threatened Iran's civilian infrastructure, warning that the US would destroy a bridge or power plant every time Tehran attacked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
• US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked a US Senate committee for an additional 70 billion dollars to fund the war in Iran as Senators demanded explanations of the military's strategy.
(FRANCE 24 with Reuters, AP and AFP)
new_text:
UN chief says Middle East conflict is at the 'edge of the imaginable'
Ongoing conflict in the Middle East has pushed the region to the "edge of the unimaginable", UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned on Thursday, as Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea threatened to escalate the conflict further. President Donald Trump said the US would hold Iran responsible for these attacks, as the rebels threatened a naval blockade. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.
This liveblog is no longer being updated.
This liveblog is no longer being updated.
US military completes 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran
The US military said late on Thursday it had completed its latest round of strikes on Iran, marking a 13th consecutive night of American attacks.
The latest wave of strikes lasted more than two hours, according to US Central Command.
US military launches 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran
The United States military said on Thursday it was attacking Iran for the 13th night in a row.
"US forces started another night of strikes against Iranian military targets at 6:45 p.m. ET (2245 GMT) today," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said, adding that the "strikes aimed to hold Iran accountable and diminish threats from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to commercial shipping."
Trump says US will use frozen Iranian assets to cover shipping damage
President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US would begin using frozen Iranian assets to pay for ships and cargo damaged by strikes in and around the Gulf.
"Please let this statement serve to represent, until further notice, that from this point forth, any and all damages done to Ships, Cargo, or anything related thereto, will be paid for by Iranian Money that the United States has in its possession, and controls," Trump said on Truth Social.
Kuwait says under attack by Iranian missiles and drones
Kuwaiti air defence batteries opened fire on incoming Iranian missiles and drones on Thursday, the Gulf country's armed forces announced.
"Kuwaiti air defences are currently intercepting hostile missile and drone attacks following the wrongful Iranian aggression," the general staff said in a message posted on social media.
IMO chief condemns attacks on shipping in the Red Sea area
The head of the International Maritime Organization on Thursday condemned the latest reported attacks
on international shipping in the Red Sea area.
Yemen's Houthi militia attacked two Saudi Arabian oil tankers in a military operation, the group said on Thursday, and a Saudi news agency later confirmed one of the two vessels was ablaze after an assault while sailing in the Red Sea.
"I unequivocally condemn the latest reported attacks on international shipping in the Red Sea area," IMO's Arsenio Dominguez said, adding that he is also concerned about the potential pollution from such incidents in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz area.
Iran media reports US strike on Qeshm Island in Hormuz
Iranian news outlet Tasnim reports that a US missile had hit a site near the town of Suza on Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz.
"The relevant authorities are currently assessing the extent of the incident and the possible level of damage," the agency said.
Houthi blockade could present a 'second big problem for world trade'
The Houthi threat to blockade the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a crucial passage into the Red Sea, as part of a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, could present a "second big problem for world trade," explains FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani.
While the Yemen-based Houthis have attempted to separate their naval blockade on Saudi Arabia from the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz , it effectively threatens shipping on both sides of the Arabian Peninsula.
It also comes at a bad time for the Trump administration, adds Gorjesthani. "It's clear that for the Americans and for this administration, the political timing is not on their side because you have the midterms coming up in November and we know that this war is, by and large, unpopular," she notes.
UK says armed forces ready to defend country after Iran warning over US bombers
Britain said on Thursday its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack
after Iran's Revolutionary Guards issued a warning over allowing US bombers to fly from UK bases.
"Our Armed Forces are ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it's on our soil or from
abroad. The UK stands ready 24/7 to defend itself," a government spokesperson said.
"This includes through operating a layered approach to air and missile defence, provided by Royal Navy, British Army and
Royal Air Force assets equipped with a range of advanced capabilities, working closely with our NATO allies," they added.
US Senate blocks resolution curbing Trump's Iran war powers
The US Senate has blocked a Democratic-led resolution aiming to stop the Iran war until hostilities are authorised by Congress. The resolution reflects growing congressional concern, even among President Donald Trump's Republicans, over the war.
The Senate voted 49 to 47 not to advance the war powers resolution.
The Senate vote came hours after the House of Representatives backed the resolution directing Trump to halt US military action against Iran unless he obtains Congress's approval.
Trump tells Axios he is considering restarting major combat operations in Iran
President Donald Trump has told Axios in an interview that he is seriously considering restarting major combat operations in Iran, which could include larger strikes than those carried out during "Operaton Epic Fury," the news outlet reported.
"They haven't received enough pain yet," Axios quoted Trump as saying, adding that Trump said he had not yet made a final decision.
Three killed after two stabbing attacks in West Bank, Israeli army says
Three Palestinians were killed after two stabbing attacks in the north of the occupied West Bank, one near an Israeli settlement and another near an army base, the military said.
In the first incident, two Palestinians were killed near the Itamar settlement when an Israeli spotted them attacking an Israeli civilian, the Israeli army said, adding that the Israeli civilian "eliminated" the two Palestinians, without specifying how they were killed.
In a separate incident on Thursday, the Israeli military said soldiers killed a Palestinian who committed a stabbing attack near the former Israeli settlement of Ganim, where Israel has recently established a military base.
"A suspicious vehicle drove through the Ganim area... and approached the military post, where an IDF soldier on guard duty was standing nearby," before its driver stabbed the soldier in the leg, the army said.
The Palestinian health ministry identified the deceased man as Yazan Sawafteh, 25.
US House again passes resolution seeking to halt military action in Iran
The US House has narrowly passed a resolution to halt US military action in Iran, sending a warning to President Donald Trump for the second time as the Iran war has escalated and the future of the conflict is increasingly uncertain.
The 214-208 vote requiring congressional approval for the war comes as the US Senate is expected to consider a similar resolution later Thursday.
Though the votes forced by Democrats are largely symbolic, they are meant as a strong signal to the Republican president that his support on Capitol Hill is chipping away as the war drags on and lawmakers in both parties have questioned his administration's endgame.
The resolution narrowly passed after a handful of Republicans voted with Democrats to end the war. But the vast majority of Republicans voted to back the war and cede congressional war powers to Trump.
Trump has insisted that continued US attacks against Iran do not mean a return to war or long-term action.
Mideast situation on 'edge of the unimaginable', UN chief warns
The current conflict in the Middle East has pushed the region to the "edge of the unimaginable", UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has warned.
"The situation is getting out of control. It is teetering on the edge of the unimaginable. The region is being pulled into an ever-widening circle of confrontation. One crisis feeds another. One escalation triggers the next," Guterres told a Security Council meeting.
"As this dynamic spreads, the political objectives are becoming increasingly obscured by the confrontation itself."
Hezbollah says Lebanon president's US visit a 'submission to foreign tutelage'
Hezbollah has called Lebanese President Joseph Aoun's recent visit to Washington a failure and said it showed the government's submission to a foreign power.
In a statement, the group's lawmakers said the visit revealed "the extent of subservience and submission to foreign tutelage", adding that it "failed to achieve... an American commitment to the withdrawal of the enemy from our land", referring to Israel.
The statement came two days after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met President Donald Trump at the White House, where he "stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory".
Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon's army is to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from "pilot zones" where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.
Palestinian Authority raises alarm as Israeli banks plan to cut ties
Israeli banks have informed their Palestinian counterparts that they intend to end critical banking services within weeks, said Palestinian and Israeli officials, raising fears of an economic crisis in the West Bank.
These banking links are essential for financing imports from Israel to the occupied Palestinian territory, including electricity, water, fuel and food, as well as for transferring wages earned by Palestinians working in Israel.
"This is not simply a technical banking matter. These channels are a cornerstone of the infrastructure that underpins our trade, our commerce, and the daily life of millions of people," Palestinian Monetary Authority governor Yahya Shunnar told journalists.
Israel's finance ministry has confirmed that two banks had proposed cutting ties with their Palestinian counterparts.
"In light of the overall risk environment and the growing concern over private lawsuits against banking entities, the Israeli banks recently announced their intention to discontinue providing correspondent banking services," the ministry said on Wednesday.
Israel says Saudi joining Abrahams Accords would be 'historic' for regional peace
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office has said Saudi Arabia's recognition of Israel would be a significant step towards peace in the Middle East.
"Saudi Arabia's joining of the Abraham Accords would be a historic leap forward for peace in the Middle East", Netanyahu's office said after President Donald Trump announced that a US-Saudi nuclear deal would be contingent on the kingdom recognising Israel.
How Houthi strikes on oil tankers will impact the Middle East war
Yemen's Houthi rebels say they have attacked two Saudi oil tankers. The Houthis are supported by Iran, and the attacks in the Red Sea could be a new front for the war between the US and Iran. How will this affect the conflict?
France calls on Houthis to stop attacks on Saudi tankers
France has called on the Houthi to stop their attacks on Saudi tankers, saying that the strikes marked a major escalation and were irresponsible.
"Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers are irresponsible and a serious escalation," a spokesperson for the French foreign ministry told reporters at a news conference.
The Iran-backed Houthis struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea earlier today as part of a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, threatening to create a second chokepoint on global oil supplies alongside the near closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
• President Donald Trump attended a dignified transfer of remains ceremony at a military base in Delaware for four US service members killed in the Iran war. Of the four slain soldiers, three were killed in an Iranian missile attack on a military base in Jordan and another died in a separate incident in northern Iraq.
• Trump threatened Iran's civilian infrastructure, warning that the US would destroy a bridge or power plant every time Tehran attacked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
• US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth asked a US Senate committee for an additional 70 billion dollars to fund the war in Iran as Senators demanded explanations of the military's strategy.
(FRANCE 24 with Reuters, AP and AFP)
